title: Asia's AI Chip Stocks Crash: Kospi Sinks 6% as Doubts Over the AI Boom Return
yt_title: Asia's AI Chip Stocks Crash: Kospi -6%, Samsung & SK Hynix Plunge | AI News
yt_description:
AI and chip stocks tumbled across Asia on Wednesday, November 25. South Korea's Kospi sank about 6%, Taiwan's Taiex fell as much as 7.9% in morning trading, and Samsung, SK Hynix, Tokyo Electron, Advantest and SoftBank took double-digit hits, just one day after Nvidia's record 31.5% jump. Why are investors nervous about the AI boom again? Here's the quick version.

script: Welcome to IT News, AI News! Today, Asia's AI chip stocks fell off a cliff. On Wednesday, South Korea's Kospi index sank about six percent. Ouch! Taiwan's Taiex dropped as much as seven point nine percent in morning trading. Japan's Nikkei slid roughly three percent, while Hong Kong barely moved. The chip giants got hit hardest. Samsung and SK Hynix each lost around ten percent. In Japan, chip tool makers Tokyo Electron and Advantest fell more than thirteen percent. SoftBank Group dropped almost fifteen percent, and memory maker Kioxia about fourteen. Taiwan's TSMC and Foxconn were deep in the red too. Not a great day to check your portfolio. It all started on Wall Street. On Monday, Nvidia soared thirty one and a half percent, after Jensen Huang returned as CEO. But on Tuesday, Nvidia gave back almost six percent, and the Nasdaq fell one and a half percent. Even newcomer Anthropic slipped below its eighty three dollar IPO price, just days after listing. So why the panic? Investors still doubt that AI will earn enough money to pay for all those data centers. There are also worries about tougher AI rules after the US midterms, and about new tariffs. And high interest rates make borrowing for giant AI projects more expensive. Not everything fell, though. India's Sensex actually jumped more than two percent! Is the AI boom wobbling, or is this just a bumpy ride? Read the full story on itnewsainews dot xpigeon dot net!
